steps: EMERGENCY — urgent whole-spine MRI; immobilise if traumatic/unstable.
High-dose dexamethasone for malignant compression (with PPI).
Emergency referral to spinal surgery / oncology for decompression ± radiotherapy.
Time-critical: outcome depends on speed — treat within hours.

drugRefs.dose: 16 mg daily (e.g. 8 mg twice daily; some give a 10 mg IV loading dose)
drugRefs.freq: once daily (or 8 mg twice daily), reduced/tapered after definitive treatment
drugRefs.why: Reduces vasogenic cord oedema and can improve neurological function while awaiting surgery/radiotherapy. Give gastric protection alongside.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Neoplastic Spinal Cord Compression
NICE NG234 — Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression in Adults
EFNS/EANO Guidance on Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression

drugRefs.freq: once daily while on high-dose corticosteroid
drugRefs.why: Reduces steroid-associated gastric/peptic ulcer risk during high-dose dexamethasone.
Immobile patients with malignancy are at high VTE risk; use prophylactic-dose LMWH unless contraindicated.

refs: NICE NG234 — Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression in Adults

confirm: Bilateral leg weakness, a sensory level, and bladder/bowel dysfunction ± back pain. Urgent whole-spine MRI.
